lessons.title: Question: Display Flex
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens if we apply the display: flex property on a child of an existing flex container?

It becomes a flex container in addition to being the flex child of its parent containerIt gets reset to display: blockIt doesn't get reset

It becomes a flex container in addition to being the flex child of its parent container.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A card is already a child of a flex container. You add display: flex to the card itself. What two roles does the card now have?

It remains a flex item and also becomes a flex container.It stops being a flex item because it is now a flex container.It becomes a block element again.

It remains a flex item and also becomes a flex container.

lessons.title: Question: Parent and child
lessons.interactiveContent:
Is the <h2> element a flexbox parent or a flexbox child?

In this case, the <h2> element is a flexbox childIn this case, the <h2> element is a flexbox parentThe <h2> element is not affected in any way

In this case, the <h2> element is a flexbox child.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The container has display: flex. Which shown element is one of its direct flex items?

The <h2> element containing Whiskers.The <body> element.The stylesheet link in <head>.

The <h2> element containing Whiskers.

lessons.title: Question: All elements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Based on the code below, how many flex rows will appear on the page?

One rowTwo rowsIt depends on whether it's viewed on mobile or not

One row.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You add flex-direction: column-reverse; to .container. How will the two paragraphs appear?

First paragraph below Another paragraph.First paragraph above Another paragraph.Side by side, with First paragraph on the right.

First paragraph below Another paragraph.

lessons.title: Example: Wider content
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the content so that the flex items overflow the container.

Make sure to pick #havingthebesttimeeveronthebeach.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Code the content so that the flex items overflow the container.

Use the long beach hashtag in the first item so it cannot fit like the short tags.

Make sure to pick #havingthebesttimeeveronthebeach.

lessons.title: Question: Width
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the default width of a flex item?

The width of its parentThe width of its contentThe width of the browser window

The width of its content.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A flex container is much wider than a label inside it, and no width is set on the item. What determines the item's initial width?

The width of the item's content.The full width of the parent container.The width of the browser window.

The width of the item's content.

lessons.title: Question: Flex-direction
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we control whether the flex items will line up horizontally or vertically?

Using the flex-direction propertyUsing the flex-axis propertyWe can't control it

Using the flex-direction property.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You want the children of a flex container to stack vertically instead of side by side. Which property controls that change?

flex-directionflex-axisflex-layout

Make sure to pick flex-direction.

lessons.title: Question: Default value
lessons.interactiveContent:
How can we tell, from the code below, that the flex-direction property is set to row?

Because it's the default value and so we don't have to specify itBecause it is set somewhere else in the codeBecause this property is never set by the developer

Because it's the default value and so we don't have to specify it.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The container is a flex container, but no flex-direction declaration appears. Which direction does the browser use by default?

rowcolumnNo direction until one is declared.

Make sure to pick row.

lessons.title: Question: Stretch
lessons.interactiveContent:
Based on the code below, how wide will each of the flex items be?

300 pixels200 pixels100 pixels

300 pixels.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You add margin: 10px; to .item. How wide will each item be, including its borders but excluding margins?

280 pixels.300 pixels.75 pixels.

280 pixels.

lessons.title: Example: Column reverse
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display items in a column, with number 1 on the bottom, number 2 in the middle, and number 3 on top.

Make sure to pick flex followed by direction and then column, reverse.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Display items in a column, with number 1 on the bottom, number 2 in the middle, and number 3 on top.

Complete the direction so the items use a vertical main axis in reverse order.

Make sure to pick container, followed by flex, flex-direction, and finally column-reverse.

lessons.title: Example: Column reverse explanation
lessons.interactiveContent:
With flex-direction set to column-reverse, place the lowest number on the top, and the largest number on the bottom.

Make sure to pick nine, followed by eight, and finally seven.

lessons.title: Question: Cross axis
lessons.interactiveContent:
Pick the correct definition of the main axis.

The main axis is an imaginary line parallel to the cross axisThe main axis is an imaginary line perpendicular to the cross axisThe main axis is an imaginary line that runs diagonally to the cross axis

The main axis is an imaginary line perpendicular to the cross axis.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If the cross axis runs vertically through a flex container, how does the main axis run relative to it?

Horizontally, perpendicular to the cross axis.Vertically, parallel to the cross axis.Diagonally across the cross axis.

Horizontally, perpendicular to the cross axis.

lessons.title: Question: Cross row
lessons.interactiveContent:
In which case is the cross axis vertical?

The cross axis can't be verticalThe cross axis is diagonalWhen flex-direction is set to row or row-reverse

When flex-direction is set to row or row-reverse.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You change flex-direction from row-reverse to column. What happens to the cross axis?

It changes from vertical to horizontal, starting on the left.It stays vertical but now starts at the bottom.It stays vertical and starts at the top.

It changes from vertical to horizontal, starting on the left.

lessons.title: Example: Row
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the correct CSS class to make the cross axis vertical.

Make sure to type flex-row.

lessons.title: Question: Start and end
lessons.interactiveContent:
Pick the CSS declaration which will make the cross axis start from the left.

flex-direction: columnflex-direction: rowBoth are true

flex-direction: column.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You need the cross axis to begin at the left edge of the container. Which declaration makes that possible?

flex-direction: columnflex-direction: rowflex-direction: row-reverse

Make sure to pick flex-direction: column.

lessons.title: Example: Row 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the correct CSS class to make the main axis horizontal and the cross axis vertical.

Make sure to pick row-reverse.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Add the correct CSS class to make the main axis horizontal and the cross axis vertical.

Apply the class that reverses a horizontal row, rather than the one that reverses a vertical column.

Make sure to pick row-reverse.
